title: Redwood discovery — model selection (Lyra Systems)
summary: Discovery call focused on Lyra's model selection constraints for a multilingual customer-support assistant. Key themes: need for 32k+ context for long conversation & knowledge base context, strong multilingual support (EN/ES/PT/FR), tool-calling for DB lookup and ticket creation, evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private due to data residency and encryption needs. Redwood AE/SE to share pricing, performance benchmarks, security docs and run a short benchmark/pilot with sample prompts.
next_steps: Redwood to send tiered pricing and Dedicated sizing options (Maya) by 2026-12-16
Redwood SE to share model performance matrix and sample latency numbers for 8k/32k/64k contexts (Ethan) by 2026-12-16
Customer to provide 3-4 representative prompt sets and a small dataset for benchmark (Priya) by 2026-12-18
Schedule technical deep-dive trial run (SE-led) w/ Lyra infra for week of 2026-12-21
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pricing + Dedicated sizing + SLA summary — due 2026-12-16
Ethan Roberts: Share latency/throughput numbers and recommend model + quantization options — due 2026-12-16
Priya Nair: Provide sample prompts and dataset for benchmark — due 2026-12-18
Samir Patel: Confirm VPC requirements and KMS/HSM vendor info — due 2026-12-17
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-13 11:00 AM PST | Duration 55 minutes | Attendees listed above

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. quick agenda — understand your model needs, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, security and deployment preference. Ethan from our SE team will cover performance questions.
00:18 Priya Nair: thanks maya, appreciate it. short background — Lyra is building a customer support assistant for our marketplace. currently we use a combination of in-house rules + a smaller model for routing. looking to centralize on a single LLM stack that can handle long threads and external tool calls (ticket create, user lookup). main constraints are multilingual and data residency in EU.
00:40 Maya Chen: great. can you share expected scale? concurrent requests, latency SLOs?
00:46 Priya Nair: traffic estimates — start small: 50 concurrent, ramp to 500 concurrent in 6 months. latency target for interactive agent is under 800ms median, but we can allow up to 1.5s for complex responses. most important is cost predictability and security.
01:05 Alex Gomez: also need 30,000 to 60,000 token context for long conversation + knowledge snippets from KB. Some of our support threads include full chat history plus product docs. We want model to be able to ingest past conversation + doc context.
01:22 Ethan Roberts: ok that helps. so we should look at models that support longer context windows — there are open models with 32k and experimental 64k windows; we can also discuss Redwood kernel+kv cache strategies to handle recurring prefixes without paying full context every time.
01:41 Samir Patel: for infra — looks like we're leaning toward Private deployment because of data residency and our compliance team wants customer-managed keys. Is Redwood Private fully air-gapped option? and what integration exists for our HSM?
01:54 Maya Chen: yes, our Private offering supports VPC/on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We have SOC 2 and will provide compliance pack. For on-prem air-gapped installs, there's an enterprise engagement but possible.
02:08 Priya Nair: perfect. i know dedicated/hosted is cheaper/faster to stand up — can you help us weigh tradeoffs?
02:15 Ethan Roberts: sure. Quick breakdown: Hosted is fastest — get API keys and start, predictable request-level pricing but multi-tenant. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, better unit economics at scale and isolation — useful for 500+ concurrent. Private gives maximum control (VPC or on-prem), customer-managed keys, full audit trails and data residency. Latency differences depend on proximity and instance sizing; Dedicated can be tuned for guaranteed throughput.
02:40 Alex Gomez: model selection — we evaluate open models (Mistral, Llama-variants, Mistral ×, Mistral-Open, and some community 32k/64k variants). Do you have Redwood-verified performance for these? especially for multilingual (EN/ES/PT/FR) and tool-calling reliability?
02:58 Ethan Roberts: we maintain a model catalog with vetted open models and performance profiles. For multilingual, some models are noticeably better in certain languages; we can share a matrix showing accuracy and token costs per language. Tool-calling is mostly model-independent from an API perspective — Redwood supports function/tool-calling primitives and structured outputs; though some models handle structured prompts better.
03:18 Priya Nair: when you say tool-calling primitives, do you mean function calling like json schema responses or a separate tool-runner? We need reliable determinism for ticket create flows.
03:29 Maya Chen: both — streaming structured outputs + function-calling helpers. We expose a call pattern where the model returns a structured payload and Redwood runtime can invoke configured tool endpoints with retries, idempotency guards, and tracing. SE will run through specifics in the trial.
03:44 Alex Gomez: on context length, how do you handle 60k? we can't send full 60k each time — cost will spike.
03:51 Ethan Roberts: good point. two approaches: 1) use a model variant that natively supports 64k; 2) combine KV prefix caching + document retrieval: keep the stable parts (user profile, common KB excerpts) cached on the runtime KV so you don't re-send them; only pull dynamic segments. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and caching parameters to reduce token cost. We also have quantization/compilation profiles to keep latency low.
04:20 Samir Patel: any noise about hallucinations with longer contexts? we need high precision for ticket actions.
04:26 Ethan Roberts: hallucinations often relate to prompt design and grounding. For actions like ticket create, we prefer using structured function calls validated against a schema, plus verification steps (confirm fields). Also you can run a lightweight reranker or verifier step; Redwood supports multi-step pipelines.
04:44 Lina Flores: multilingual fallback — if we detect Spanish, do you route to a Spanish-optimized model or use a single multilingual model? what's recommended?
04:53 Ethan Roberts: depends — routing to a language-optimized model can improve quality and reduce cost if that model is smaller and strong in the language. Alternatively, a single multilingual model simplifies ops but might be larger. We can propose a hybrid: detect language then route to either a Spanish-optimized model for Spanish, Portuguese models for PT, else fallback to EN multilingual model. Redwood smart routing can do that by policy.
05:17 Alex Gomez: curious about latency numbers. what's median token latency for 8k vs 32k vs 64k on Dedicated?
05:23 Ethan Roberts: i'll share measured medians in the matrix but rough order: 8k context on a quantized 8-bit profile ~50-120ms per token (depending on GPU); 32k jumps due to KV management and attention changes — roughly 2-3x per-token at similar throughput, 64k can be increase further. But pipeline parallelism and kernel selection reduce wall-time; we need to run a benchmark with your prompts.
05:47 Priya Nair: security questions — SSO, RBAC, audit logs, retention policies, and encryption. Are logs available for private deployment?
05:56 Maya Chen: yes. For Private, logs are customer-controlled. We integrate with SAML/SSO, offer role-based access, and retention policies configurable. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can provide SOC2 artifacts.
06:08 Samir Patel: also want to confirm that Redwood can run in our EU region and data doesn't leave jurisdiction for Private, right?
06:14 Maya Chen: correct — Private/VPC can be confined to your region and our control plane can be located per agreement; we'll detail options in the security pack.
06:23 Alex Gomez: about model licensing — any restrictions licensing-wise for running Llama variants or Mistral in Private?
06:28 Ethan Roberts: licensing differs by model; we annotate license types in our catalog and will flag any usage restrictions. For Private deployments, you also need to ensure compliance with model license terms; Redwood helps with that documentation.
06:40 Priya Nair: demo/pilot — what would a practical POC look like?
06:44 Maya Chen: typical pilot: Redwood provisions a Dedicated or Private trial, we ingest sample dataset, run 1-2 weeks of benchmarks across candidate models (8k/32k/64k contexts), measure latency, cost, and quality on your prompt sets. We also validate tool-calling flows and integration with your ticketing system.
07:00 Priya Nair: timeline wise — we want an internal decision by end of January. So pilot next week could work.
07:07 Maya Chen: sounds good. we'll aim for a quick start. Ethan will reach out to coordinate infra details.
07:13 Ethan Roberts: quick note — for cost control, we'll show you batching/auto-scaling policies and quantization tradeoffs. For example, using int8 or int4 quant profiles reduces memory and cost with small quality tradeoffs; we'll show per-model recommendations.
07:33 Alex Gomez: also interested in model explainability — can Redwood surface attention or token-level debugging for debugging hallucinations?
07:41 Ethan Roberts: not raw attention, but we provide token-level latency/cost traces, outputs, and trace hooks for structured evaluation including reranker scores and provenance chains. We can also store per-request metadata in the audit logs for later analysis.
08:00 Lina Flores: are there any known gotchas when switching from hosted to private later? like different API endpoints or breaking changes?
08:08 Maya Chen: API contract is the same across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; there are deployment-specific configs (networking, key management). We aim for a consistent developer experience so code changes should be minimal.
08:22 Priya Nair: ok i'm happy with that. can you confirm pricing cadence for Dedicated? we prefer a monthly committed capacity model.
08:29 Maya Chen: yes Dedicated supports monthly/annual reserved capacity with burst options. we'll include an example commit for your projected 500 concurrent target and options for autoscaling and burst capacity.
08:45 Samir Patel: for pilot we need an IP allowlist and a test VPC; i'll provide network contacts.
08:50 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll loop Ethan in and create a short checklist.
08:57 Maya Chen: quick recap of next steps — i'll send pricing and security docs, ethan will share perf matrix, priya will send prompt sets, samir will confirm infra details. any other items?
09:11 Priya Nair: nothing else, thanks team. excited to run the pilot.
09:17 Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email with calendar invites for the trial kickoff.
09:22 End of recording
